metric_dictionary.name: Customer health
metric_dictionary.definition: A 0–100 rule-based score built from product events, recognized revenue, support burden, failed invoices, and lifecycle stage.
metric_dictionary.caveat: This is not an ML model or a validated churn probability.

metric_dictionary.name: Churn risk
metric_dictionary.definition: A 0–100 rule-based risk score derived from the health score with billing, high-priority support, and churned-lifecycle adjustments.
metric_dictionary.caveat: The repository contains no model-derived churn signal.

metric_dictionary.name: Recognized revenue
metric_dictionary.definition: Invoice amount counted only when invoice status is paid and amount is positive.
metric_dictionary.caveat: The source generator intentionally includes negative invoice amounts and failed invoices.

metric_dictionary.name: Failed invoice amount
metric_dictionary.definition: Invoice amount attached to records whose billing status is failed.
metric_dictionary.caveat: Review the quality audit before using this for automated collections decisions.

metric_dictionary.name: Feature variety
metric_dictionary.definition: Average number of distinct non-null event names used by an account per active usage day.
metric_dictionary.caveat: Null event names are retained in the audit and excluded from distinct feature counts.

metric_dictionary.name: Adoption rate
metric_dictionary.definition: Accounts with at least one event for a feature divided by modeled accounts in the segment.
metric_dictionary.caveat: Event presence is a usage proxy, not proof of business value.

metric_dictionary.name: Gross revenue retention
metric_dictionary.definition: One minus churned recognized revenue divided by recognized revenue, grouped by segment and plan.
metric_dictionary.caveat: This demo does not model expansion, contraction, or renewal cohorts.

lineage.logic: Duplicate account IDs are reduced to the latest created_at record in staging.
Paid positive invoices contribute recognized_revenue; failed invoices contribute failed_invoice_amount.
Events are grouped by account and usage date; null event names remain visible to quality checks.
High and urgent tickets are marked as high priority and summarized by account.
The existing 0–100 formula combines observed account, usage, revenue, support, billing, and lifecycle inputs.
The existing 0–100 formula adds deterministic billing, high-priority support, and churned-lifecycle adjustments.
